video_title: Dirk Nowitzki & Steve Nash Talk 90s NBA Fashion + CRAZY All-Time Teammates Starting 5!

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on the evolution of point guard play
quotes.excerpt: This generation, the last two, three generations, it's the first line of attack.
quotes.quote: Just looking at the two of us, Jalen grew up more in a generation, probably shifted during your childhood, but when I grew up, a point guard, your dad is a great example, I played against Jalen's dad in the NCAA tournament, he's a great example, classic point guard: run the team, make the passes, score if you need to. That was the job of a point guard. I think this generation, the last two, three generations, it's the first line of attack. Why are we waiting around? Try to, especially in pace and space, let's try to break the defense down before it gets set and score. So to me, that is number one for our position. I think the culture of the game has changed around the position. Analytics has driven that in many ways. Also the amount of athletes that I think that weren't point guards that have become point guards in the league.

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson on how point guard roles have evolved
quotes.excerpt: People don't understand how small the court becomes in the playoffs.
quotes.quote: I feel like that's one thing I feel like, especially playoff time, people don't understand how small the court becomes in the playoffs. And like for me, that was my first series, we played Cleveland. We won, and then I got to Miami, and I think I was probably shooting like 33 or 34% that year, and Spo was just like, he's in the corner. All right, just be the block. And I was just sitting there, and I'm like, damn, like I can shoot F, and he's happy if I, if I go, if I shoot, he doesn't care if I make four, because if I make four, that means he's not getting the ball, Julius isn't getting the ball, so it's just, after that I'm like, okay, I got to like, I've worked on it, but I got to try to do a little bit more of like the mechanics.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki on the evolution of big men in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: The evolution of the bigs when we first got in the league, 90s and 90s, the fours and the fives were bigs.
quotes.quote: I would definitely say the skill level of the bigs has been incredible to watch. The evolution of the bigs when we first got in the league, 90s and 90s, the fours and the fives were bigs. If the four could stretch the elbow, that would be a stretch four. And just rebound, our bigs, run a ton of cross screens, and so then the game has changed once they start putting in the five-second back-down rule, they put in some zones, so things started shifting. And you know, now it's just everybody has to spread the floor, shoot the ball, bring the ball up, some fours, fives initiate offense, bring it up, or the guard is denied, all, I'll run the, I'll run the point guard spot for a position or two. So, yeah, I feel like the skill level, just watch Jokic can do anything on the court for, for bigs, it's just been, it's been incredible to watch, so I'm super proud of being a small part of maybe, you know, the evolution of, of the bigs.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on the importance of sacrifice for team success
quotes.excerpt: It's not what, it's who. It's sometimes it's not what you're doing, it's who you're doing it with.
quotes.quote: When you get older, and maybe you guys feel this way, it's not what, it's who. It's sometimes it's not what you're doing, it's who you're doing it with. And to do it with Dirk, first of all, our families are tight, to be on a team with Blake, UD, and Taylor, who runs the show, she's amazing, point guard, talk about a point guard, and then everyone behind the camera, it's like, man, that's a team I like, that's why I'm doing this now, because we have such a good group. And on air, I just want to see everyone have fun and succeed. It feels natural, you know what I mean? It's not like anyone's trying to like get to the top, so to speak.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki reflects on his greatest teammates and point guards
quotes.excerpt: Incredible how he saw the game, his IQ for the game.
quotes.quote: I got to start with Steve. I played with Jason Kidd, another Hall of Famer. I got to him when he was a little later in his career, but just wicked smart and just such a competitor. Incredible how he saw the game, his IQ for the game. So that'll be my two. I mean, Luka Doncic, I caught at the bare end, but obviously Hall of Famer as well. So that's three guards already.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki praises Michael Finley as an incredible teammate
quotes.excerpt: He was the man when we first got to Dallas.
quotes.quote: One of my obviously best teammates was Michael Finley. He was the man when we first got to Dallas, and then he saw Steve and I get better and better and then instead of holding us down, saying this is still my team, he kind of let us grow beside him and even pass him at some points, and he was just happy and supportive and a great, great teammate and learned so much from his constant pro, his work ethic.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki on Steve Nash's evolution and leadership
quotes.excerpt: I was so happy when he left Dallas to see how he improved and take his game to another level
quotes.quote: I was so happy when he left Dallas to see how he improved and take his game to another level that I'd never saw was capable of. One of the best teammates, I think he knows this, and leaders. If you guys spent some time with him, he's always positive, he was always encouraging. So that's why he's one of the best leaders I think the game has ever seen. His creativity, his IQ, his passing, he scored when he had to, he was clutch.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on his departure from Dallas and playoff motivation
quotes.excerpt: I felt like the castoff, like nobody wanted me, the unloved child in a way
quotes.quote: I felt like the castoff, like nobody wanted me, the unloved child in a way. And so to play them in the playoffs that year, there was some hot sauce on it. I think I hit a three, dribble down three, one of those games to win it. I can't remember what game it was, but because I felt like they discarded me, that was an important series for me, as much as I didn't like to admit it.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on the differences between NBA and international basketball
quotes.excerpt: The biggest one is the rules for me, it's a different game
quotes.quote: The biggest one is the rules for me, it's a different game. Court's a little smaller, the three-point line's a little closer, there's no three seconds in the lane, 2.9. The refs also call things differently. You can't put a hand in a face, and there's different things like that. If you flop, you get a warning, and then you get a technical. So there are things like that, which we should be doing in the NBA, we don't really do. So I think right there, that changes the way we play.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki on the differences in international basketball coaching
quotes.excerpt: There's a lot more of that stuff, like in the EuroLeague or internationally
quotes.quote: There's a lot more of that stuff, like in the EuroLeague or internationally. There's more sets, balls changing sides, there's cute actions going on, there's a counter, there's a misdirection. So I think there's a lot more of that stuff, like in the EuroLeague or internationally. It's a little bit more play-calling that it is straight, I go at this guy, I call this guy up, he's going to switch and now I go in my bag. It's a little bit more team play.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki clarifies Nikola Jokic's comments on international basketball
quotes.excerpt: I don't think he means they should go over there and learn how to play
quotes.quote: I saw what Jokic was trying to say and some of the guys got offended, but I don't think he means they should go over there and learn how to play. I don't think that's what he was trying to say. He was trying to say you should see the passion that a EuroLeague game, what's going on, and just because they were asking him also about pressures, like, dude, I played in front of 20,000 people throwing stuff at me, so I think that's more what he meant.
